subject: StellarHealth redline: subprocessor/runtime access — product/security assessment requested
messages:
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@stellarhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: 2027-11-10T15:22:00Z
Subject: Contract redline: runtime access / subprocessors (StellarHealth DPA)

Hi Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team sent back a DPA with a few redlines that touch runtime/data-use and subprocessors. The main asks are:

- No cross-tenant KV caching: clause now says Redwood must ensure no opportunity for data from one StellarHealth tenant to be accessible to another tenant (they redlined a strict prohibition).
- Subprocessor freeze: they want the right to a 30-day notice and approval for any runtime subprocessor that has access to inference logs or telemetry that could include customer data.
- Telemetry export restrictions: any telemetry related to inference outputs must be stored in-region and encrypted with a customer-controlled key.

I attached the redlines (StellarHealth_DPA_Redlines.pdf) — legal flagged these as deal-blocking unless we can provide product/security options or language to compromise.

Can your product/security teams assess the impact (cost, roadmap delta, rollout timeline) and propose alternate language we can send back? They asked for a response within 5 business days.

Thanks —
Sara Liu
Senior PM, StellarHealth

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Contract redline: runtime access / subprocessors (StellarHealth DPA)

Thanks Sara — looping in Product and Security.

Quick internal notes for triage teams:
- The explicit ban on cross-tenant KV caching as written would force us to disable our global prefix caching optimization for this customer and potentially for any other customer that requires this protection (or we maintain a separate isolated runtime per-tenant). Both have cost and latency impacts.
- Subprocessor freeze (30-day approval) intersects with our normal vendor rotation/patching cadence. We currently publish a subprocessor list with 14-day notice for certain infra changes.
- Customer-controlled KMS + in-region telemetry: achievable but will add operational overhead (KMS integration per-account, changes to telemetry pipelines).

Can Product (Marissa) provide: a short impact statement (latency/cost, ETA to support per-tenant KV namespace, effort to support per-customer KMS) and a recommended alternative clause we can propose?
Can Security (Olga) provide: required controls and minimum evidence we can provide to the customer to satisfy their ask without agreeing to a hard ban?

I've started a quick triage checklist attached. I'll flag to Legal if we need leadership escalation.

Thanks —
Jonas
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-12T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Contract redline: runtime access / subprocessors (StellarHealth DPA)

Thanks Jonas — wrote up product's quick impact assessment below.

TL;DR: we should avoid a blanket "no cross-tenant KV cache" prohibition. Recommended alternative: agree to a technical guarantee that StellarHealth's tenant data will be logically and cryptographically isolated (per-tenant KV namespaces + encryption-at-rest using per-tenant keys), plus an audit/logging commitment. Offer a migration/feature rollout plan with timelines rather than a permanent disabled-state.

Impact details (ballpark):
- Per-tenant KV namespace: engineering estimate 6–10 wks of focused work to make namespace isolation first-class across runtime and billing; initial rollout gated to Dedicated/Private deployments, with a later hosted API opt-in. Implementation adds ~8–12% higher per-token CPU cost due to loss of shared cache efficiency.
- Disable shared cache globally for StellarHealth only: quick (1–2 wks) but increases token cost by ~18–25% for their workload; avoids full product changes but is operationally heavy to maintain as an exception.
- Customer KMS for telemetry: moderate work (4–6 wks) to integrate per-customer KMS for telemetry bucket encryption and restrict cross-region exports. Will require added E2E testing and SRE runbook changes.

Suggested contract language (draft text to send to StellarHealth legal):
"We will ensure logical isolation of StellarHealth tenant data by implementing per-tenant KV namespaces and encryption-at-rest. Redwood will provide audit logs demonstrating isolation and will not intentionally route StellarHealth tenant requests to other customers. Redwood reserves the right to route requests across compatible infrastructure for operational resilience; prior to deploying any routing that could affect data isolation, Redwood will notify the customer and provide mitigation controls."

I attached a draft proposal doc with more details and an initial timeline. If Security can confirm the minimum controls they require, we can ship this back to Sara as a compromise that avoids a blunt ban.

Proposed next steps:
1) Security to confirm controls and evidence list (Olga).
2) Product to prepare one-page cost/latency delta for Legal and Procurement.
3) If customer requires per-tenant KMS or a subprocessor approval window beyond our policy, escalate to Leadership for approval on concession and pricing.

-Marissa
Director, Product (Inference)
Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, sara.liu@stellarhealth.com, procurement@stellarhealth.com
Date: 2027-11-14T11:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Contract redline: runtime access / subprocessors (StellarHealth DPA)

Appreciate the write-up, Marissa — Security's position below.

We can accept an alternative to a categorical ban if the following minimum controls are contractually required and technically verifiable:
- Per-tenant keying for any persistent KV/cache that could contain customer-derived content; keys must be customer-provided (KMS) or a mutually agreed KMS configuration with separate key material per tenant.
- Runtime isolation guarantee: Redwood will provide a documented architecture diagram and audit logs showing namespace separation and access controls for 90 days post-activation.
- Subprocessor notification: Redwood will provide a 30-day notice for any new subprocessor that can access inference output or telemetry for StellarHealth; for critical security patches we require a defined emergency exception process (describe in contract).
- In-region telemetry storage: telemetry that contains inference outputs tied to customer requests must be stored in the customer's region and encrypted with their keying where requested.

Suggested redline language we can offer: 
"Redwood shall maintain per-customer namespaces and cryptographic separation for any persistent inference cache or key-value store that could include customer-derived input or output. Customer shall be entitled to audit logs and evidence of separation for a period of 90 days following activation. Redwood shall provide at least 30 days' notice for the addition of any new subprocessor with access to inference output; Redwood will outline an emergency patch process that allows for accelerated deployment with immediate notice and post-deployment validation."

Evidence we can provide immediately: architecture diagram, current subprocessor list, SOC2 report section references, sample audit log (sanitized). Evidence requiring work: per-tenant KMS integration (4–6 wks) and telemetry region partitioning (additional 3–5 wks).

If StellarHealth insists on the original hard ban, we should treat as a change request and price accordingly (because it forces either dedicated runtime pools or a slower roadmap). I'm copying Grace for compliance sign-off and to confirm whether the 90-day audit log window meets our regulatory commitments.

-Olga
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks for the patience. Internal Product & Security recommend the alternative language below (attached) as a compromise to the hard ban. Summary: we will commit to per-tenant namespace isolation, provide audit logs for 90 days, and offer a 30-day subprocessor notice with an emergency patch exception. We also outlined two delivery paths (short-term exception to disable shared cache for StellarHealth; medium-term product work to implement per-tenant KV namespaces and customer KMS).

Next steps from our side:
1) I'll route the draft language through Legal and Pricing (we may need to attach a concession/price uplift if they require per-tenant dedicated runtime).
2) Marissa will prepare a one-page cost/latency delta for your procurement/legal team.
3) Olga will pull the evidence pack (SOC2 excerpts, architecture diagram, sanitized audit log).

We aim to get a formal response back to you by 2027-11-19. If you need a faster turnaround or an exec-to-exec call, let me know and we can schedule.

Best —
Jonas
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
